newsitem.title: USA: Mich. aims tax-free zones at neighboring states.
newsitem.headline: Mich. aims tax-free zones at neighboring states.

text.p: Michigan is hoping to entice businesses in neighboring states to relocate to one of its newly created Renaissance Zones that are free from most state and local taxes, a Michigan official said Thursday.
Doug Rothwell, chief executive officer of the Michigan Jobs Commission, called the zones "the mother of all business incentives."

"Michigan is the only state in the nation that can claim tax-free zones where businesses and residents pay no state or local taxes for up to 15 years," Rothwell said in a series of news releases aimed at businesses in Indiana, Illinois, Ohio and Wisconsin.

Jim Tobin, a spokesman for the jobs commission, said a $450,000 multi-media marketing campaign was planned to attract businesses to the zones. In addition, the commission intends to expand its targets beyond the Midwest to states in other regions, Tobin said.
Michigan's Administrative Board on Wednesday approved 11 sites throughout the state for the zones.
The sites will become virtually free of state income, property and business taxes, as well as local income, property and utility taxes as of Jan. 1.

State sales taxes would still be collected in the Renaissance Zones and property taxes needed to pay debt service on unlimited tax general obligation bonds issued by local governments and school districts will also be collected, state officials have said.
However, tax increment financing debt sold by downtown development authorities or special districts are not accomodated under the law, passed by the state legislature in July.
As for operating funds lost by communities, the state will replace those funds for school districts, community colleges and libraries.
The zones were designed to help distressed parts of Michigan attract jobs.

Approved sites for the zones were 120 acres in the Benton Harbor, St. Joseph, Benton Township area; 1,345 acres in Detroit; 836 acres in Flint, 536 acres in Grand Rapids; 110 acres in Lansing; 743 acres in Saginaw; 2,917 arcres in the Gogebic, Ontonagon, Houghton counties area; 556 acres in Manistee County; and 1,870 acres in Montcalm and Gratiot counties. Two former military sites in Warren and Oscodo were also picked for the zones.
